classes.subject: NTRES

notes.descrlong: Taught in Malaysia. Course fee: $2,000 payable to your bursar account to cover in-country housing, in-country transportation, activities and any travel expenses such as passports, visas, health and travel insurance, airport departure tax, necessary immunizations, and spending money. Travel dates 1/1/2020 and 1/18/2020. Permission of instructor required. Students must enroll in NTRES 4001 and NTRES 4002 to receive a final grade.

classes.description: As part of the Global Citizenship and Sustainability Program sequence, this actual in-country experience provides students with hands-on introductory experience of community-based research. In addition, students will have an exposure to the higher educational system in Malaysia, its philosophy and approach toward community-based research and the opportunity to work and learn together with UNIMAS, and UCTS students regarding sustainable development, community and cultural resilience for indigenous communities.
classes.catalogComments: Students must enroll in NTRES 4001 and NTRES 4002 to receive a final grade.
classes.catalogFee: Course fee: Students participating in the GC&S program and going abroad are responsible for a $2,000 course fee payable to your bursar account to cover in-country housing, in-country transportation, activities and any travel expenses such as passports, visas, health and travel insurance, airport departure tax, necessary immunizations, and spending money.
catalogOutcomes: Students will be able to demonstrate reflective practices (oral, written and visual), especially related to global citizenship, cultural diversity, community-based research, professional growth, leadership, and teamwork.
Students will be able to experience and learn about indigenous Malaysian cultural norms.
Students will be able to work effectively in an interdisciplinary, cross-cultural team.
Students will be able to understand local community perspectives about resilience and sustainable development in Malaysia.

classes.subject: NTRES

notes.descrlong: Taught in Washington D.C. Travel dates 1/5/2020 and 1/16/2020. First Part of Multi-term course.

classes.description: Intensive field-based exploration of the environmental policy process and its conceptual framework. Focuses on defining environmental problems; aggregating interests; agenda-setting; formulating and selecting alternative solutions; implementation and evaluation stages; and roles of lobbyists, the legislative, executive, judicial branches of government, and other actors. Discussion with policy makers as guest panelists. Research topic requires conducting independent interviews with Washington experts, policy analysis paper, and oral presentation.
classes.catalogComments: Course fee 4301: approximately $700-800 for lodging and use of facilities at the Wolpe Cornell Center in Washington, D.C. In addition to this ten-day seminar in Washington, D.C. (January 2-12, 2019), there are required preparation meetings in Ithaca during November and December. Students must enroll in both NTRES 4300 and NTRES 4301 to receive a final grade. Admission by special application process only. Completed applications due mid-October. Course information and application available online.
classes.catalogPermission: Enrollment limited to: junior, senior, or grad student standing.
catalogOutcomes: Describe a theoretical framework for policy development and implementation.
Describe, in both oral and written formats, specific examples of policy development and implementation and how they differ from theoretical frameworks.
Critically discuss how the outcomes of policy development are influenced by broader historical, economic, and social contexts.
Identify the specific ways in which various actors enter and influence the policy process.
Describe and critically discuss the role that scientific understanding and information plays in the development and implementation of policy.
